title: Sunny and the Water Reeds | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka discovers a stand of tall reeds swaying beside the moonlit billabong, their whisper filling the still night air like a gentle lullaby. A soothing bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The evening air was cool and still, except near the edge of the billabong.

There, where the water met the bank, a tall stand of reeds grew in a close, quiet row.

Little Sonny the quokka walked toward them slowly, drawn by a sound.

The reeds were singing.

Not a real song. But something that felt like one. The softest whisper of wind through thin, hollow stems.

Shsh. Shsh. Shsh.

Sunny stepped as close as she could without getting her paws wet, and she stood very still and listened.

The reeds were taller than she was. They swayed just a little — back and forth, back and forth — like they were rocking something to sleep.

She swayed too, without meaning to. Just the tiniest sway. In. And out.

The moon was reflected on the still water beyond the reeds. Silver and perfect. A whole moon made of light, resting on the surface.

A small moth landed on one reed and the reed bowed gently, then lifted again.

Sunny thought: everything here is so patient. The water. The reeds. The reflected moon. They don't hurry. They just... are.

She sat down in the soft grass at the edge of the bank and let the reed song wash over her.

Shsh. Shsh. Shsh.

The sound filled her all the way up.

She closed her eyes. She breathed out slowly.

And the gentle reed lullaby carried her off to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, water reeds. Goodnight, little one.
